To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the functional outcome of hypoglycaemic encephalopathies is poor in about 60%.
the prognosis of patients with hypoglycenic coma is poor, but that a good outcome can be expected for some patients.
prolonged hypoglycaemia is associated with a poor outcome in a majority of patients but a good outcome can be observed in some patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional outcome of comatous patients admitted to the ICU after a hypoglycematic encephalopathy, with a long-term follow up.
the causes, clinical manifestations and long-term outcome in comatose patients who are admitted in the intensive care unit due to prolonged hypoglycaemic encephalopath.
the functional outcome of patients with hypoglycemiainduced encephalopathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoglycema-induced encephalopathy is not always a poor prognostic sign.
a good outcome is possible, but rare.
the prognosis of hypoglycaemic coma is not good, although there are some exceptions to the rule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoglycemics with prolonged coma have a high risk of death or poor outcome, and the outcome is related to brain imaging and pre-ICU mRS.
patients with hypoglycemics encephalopathy have poor outcomes and the best predictor for good outcomes is the mRS score before the hypoglycemaic event.
the outcome of prolonged hypoglycaemic coma is variable and unpredictable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a long period of hypoglycaemia (>480 min) is a bad prognostic factor.

the long-term prognosis of hypoglycaemic encephalopathies is highly variable, with the best predictors of a good outcome being a normal brain imaging, a low mRS score before ICU admission and a short hypoglycemiatic duration.
the prognosis of patients with hypoglycemiarelated encephalopathy depends on the duration of hypoglycaemia, the severity of neurological status prior to ICU admission and brain imaging.
